title: ARTICLES
notes:
✓ Articles → Words placed before nouns to show whether we mean something specific or general.

✓ Three articles → a, an, the.

◆ A / An → Indefinite articles → One of many, not specific.
◆ The → Definite article → A specific or already identified noun.
◆ No article (Ø) → Used in several general and fixed expressions.

title: A — INDEFINITE ARTICLE
notes:
✓ Use 'a' before a singular countable noun when it is not specific and the following sound is a consonant sound.

◆ Examples
a book
a teacher
a car
a university
a European country

✓ The choice depends on sound, not simply spelling.

a university → /juː.../
a European → /juː.../

◆ Common uses
I saw a dog. → One dog, not a specific dog.
She is a doctor. → Profession/job.
He bought a new phone.

title: AN — INDEFINITE ARTICLE
notes:
✓ Use 'an' before a singular countable noun when the following sound is a vowel sound.

◆ Examples
an apple
an orange
an engineer
an umbrella
an hour
an honest person

✓ The choice depends on pronunciation.

an hour → h is silent.
an honest man → h is silent.

✓ Do not choose 'an' just because a word begins with a vowel letter.

❌ an university
✓ a university

title: A / AN: MAIN USES
notes:
✓ Use a/an:

◆ 1. For one person or thing when it is mentioned for the first time.
I saw a man in the street.

◆ 2. For jobs and professions.
She is a teacher.
He is an engineer.

◆ 3. To mean 'one'.
I need a pen.

◆ 4. To describe someone/something as a member of a group or class.
She is a good student.

◆ 5. In certain expressions of quantity or frequency.
twice a day
$5 a kilo
60 km an hour

title: THE — DEFINITE ARTICLE
notes:
✓ Use 'the' when the listener/reader can identify the specific person or thing being discussed.

◆ Example
I saw a dog. The dog was very large.

✓ First mention → a dog.
✓ Second/specific mention → the dog.

✓ Use 'the' when the noun is:
• already mentioned
• clearly identified by context
• unique in the situation
• made specific by additional information

title: THE: UNIQUE THINGS
notes:
✓ Use 'the' with things considered unique or clearly identifiable.

◆ Examples
the sun
the moon
the Earth
the sky
the internet

The sun is shining.
The Earth moves around the sun.

✓ Use depends on whether the noun is understood as a unique, identifiable thing.

title: THE: GEOGRAPHICAL NAMES
notes:
✓ Common geographical uses of 'the':

◆ Rivers → the Nile
◆ Seas → the Red Sea
◆ Oceans → the Indian Ocean
◆ Deserts → the Sahara
◆ Mountain ranges → the Alps
◆ Groups of islands → the Philippines
◆ Groups of states/countries → the United States, the United Kingdom

✓ Usually no 'the' with:
• individual mountains → Mount Everest
• individual lakes → Lake Victoria
• most countries → Ethiopia, Kenya, France
• most cities → Addis Ababa, Nairobi, London

title: THE: PLACES & INSTITUTIONS
notes:
✓ Use 'the' when referring to a specific building, institution, or place.

The school near my house is large.
The hospital on this street is closed.

✓ Some institutions can be used without an article when referring to their main purpose/function.

Children go to school.
He is in prison.
She went to bed.

✓ Compare:
He goes to school. → As a student.
I went to the school. → A specific school/building.

title: THE: GROUPS & CLASSES
notes:
✓ 'The + adjective' can refer to a group of people with a shared characteristic.

◆ Examples
the rich
the poor
the elderly
the unemployed

The government should support the poor.

✓ 'The + singular noun' can sometimes represent a whole species/class in formal contexts.
The lion is a powerful animal.

title: THE WITH SUPERLATIVES & ORDINALS
notes:
✓ Use 'the' with superlative adjectives.

the best student
the tallest building
the most interesting book

✓ Use 'the' with ordinal numbers.

the first day
the second chapter
the last question

✓ Also commonly used with words such as:
the only
the same
the next
the previous

✓ These expressions identify something as particular or unique within a group.

title: A / AN VS THE
notes:
✓ A/AN → Non-specific or first mention.
✓ THE → Specific or already identified.

◆ Examples
I bought a book yesterday. The book is interesting.

She wants to buy a car. → Any suitable car.
She wants to buy the car we saw yesterday. → A specific car.

✓ Quick rule →
First/general → A/AN.
Known/specific → THE.

title: ZERO ARTICLE (Ø)
notes:
✓ Zero article → No article is used before the noun.

◆ Examples
Books are useful.
Water is essential for life.
I like music.
Students need education.

✓ Commonly used with plural countable nouns and uncountable nouns when speaking generally.

Dogs are friendly. → Dogs in general.
Coffee is popular. → Coffee in general.

title: COUNTABLE VS UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS
notes:
✓ Singular countable nouns usually need a determiner.

❌ I bought book.
✓ I bought a book.
✓ I bought the book.

✓ Plural countable nouns can be general without an article.
Books are expensive.

✓ Uncountable nouns can be general without an article.
Water is important.

✓ Specific uncountable nouns can take 'the'.
The water in this bottle is cold.

title: MEALS, SPORTS & LANGUAGES
notes:
✓ Usually no article when speaking generally about meals, sports, and languages.

We had breakfast.
She plays football.
He speaks English.

✓ Use an article when the noun is made specific or modified.

The breakfast at the hotel was excellent.
The football match was exciting.
The English spoken in this region is different.

title: SUBJECTS & ACADEMIC AREAS
notes:
✓ School subjects and academic fields generally take no article when used as general names.

I study mathematics.
She likes geography.
He studies chemistry.

✓ Use 'the' when referring to a specific course, field, or context.

The mathematics of this problem is difficult.
The history of Ethiopia is fascinating.

title: FIXED EXPRESSIONS WITHOUT ARTICLES
notes:
✓ Some common expressions normally use no article.

◆ Examples
at home
at work
at school
in bed
by car
by bus
by train
go to school
go to bed

She is at home.
He goes to school by bus.
I was in bed early.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ He is teacher.
✓ He is a teacher.

❌ She is an university student.
✓ She is a university student.

❌ I bought book yesterday.
✓ I bought a book yesterday.

❌ Sun is hot.
✓ The sun is hot.

❌ I like the music. → Incorrect when speaking about music generally in this context.
✓ I like music.

❌ The Ethiopia is a country in Africa.
✓ Ethiopia is a country in Africa.

❌ He plays the football.
✓ He plays football.

✓ Always ask: Is the noun singular/countable? Is it specific? Is it general? Is the article required by the expression?

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. A → Singular countable + consonant sound.
a book, a university.

◆ 2. AN → Singular countable + vowel sound.
an apple, an hour.

◆ 3. THE → Specific, known, unique, or clearly identified noun.
the book on the table.

◆ 4. Ø → Often used for general plural and uncountable nouns.
Books are useful.
Water is important.

◆ 5. First mention → Often a/an.
I saw a bird.

◆ 6. Later/specific mention → Often the.
The bird flew away.

◆ 7. Superlatives → the best, the largest.

◆ 8. Ordinals → the first, the second, the last.

◆ 9. Jobs/professions → a/an.
She is an engineer.

◆ 10. Rivers, oceans, seas, deserts, mountain ranges → Commonly the.

✓ Golden rule → A/AN = one but not specific; THE = specific/identified; Ø = general meaning in many contexts.
